problem_statement:
Keyboard users cannot reach or scroll a wide chart's sideways-scrolling frame

Charts whose drawing is 480px (30rem) wide or more keep that width and scroll sideways inside a frame on narrow screens, instead of shrinking their text. But that frame (`div.enarratio-frame.enarratio-frame-wide`) is not focusable, so someone using only a keyboard cannot reach it and has no way to scroll the hidden part of the chart into view. The frame also has no accessible name or focus style.

Reproduce: render `barChart({ data: [{ k: "a" }], x: "k", title: "Counts", alt: "a" })` (default width 640) and inspect the frame: it has no `tabindex`, no role and no label.

Expected:
- Every wide frame is in the tab order (`tabindex="0"`), has `role="group"`, and is named from the chart's title as `"<title>, scrolls sideways"`, e.g. `"Counts, scrolls sideways"`. When the chart has no title (or a blank/whitespace title) the name is `"Chart, scrolls sideways"`; it should not reuse the alt text, which the SVG inside already announces.
- Narrow frames (e.g. `width: 300`), which never scroll, stay as they are: no tabindex and no label.
- The base stylesheet gives the frame the same `:focus-visible` outline the chart uses elsewhere (a `.enarratio-frame:focus-visible` rule).
- Once `enhance()` makes the chart's marks focusable, the frame's extra tab stop is redundant; it should be removed while enhanced and restored by `destroy()`.
fail_to_pass: npx vitest run test/review.test.ts -t "lets a keyboard reach a wide frame"
pass_to_pass: npx vitest run test/review.test.ts -t "wraps the SVG in a frame that keeps a minimum width for wide drawings only"
